title: Disjoint Borel annuli that every injective ray meets infinitely often at Borel asymptotic separation index one
source_title: Borel Edge Colorings for Finite Dimensional Groups

context_spans.label: discrete and Borel asymptotic separation index, distance N-graph and asymptotic dimension
injective G-ray, radius-n ball B(U,n) and annulus A(U,n,m)

standard_prerequisites.name: Locally finite Borel graphs and their distance graphs
standard_prerequisites.statement: A locally finite Borel graph on a standard Borel space, its distance N-graph G^{<=N}, Borel partitions, and connected components of an induced subgraph; all of this is retained from the article's own Section 2 passage at source lines 123-129
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof builds the annuli inside a Borel partition and reasons about G^{<=N}-components

standard_prerequisites.name: Borel asymptotic separation index one
standard_prerequisites.statement: asi_B(G)=1 means that for every N the space splits into two Borel pieces U_0, U_1 with G^{<=N} restricted to each piece having only finite connected components (source lines 125-127). No consequence of the invariant beyond this witnessing partition is assumed
standard_prerequisites.use: The scale N=4d+1 and the partition of X into U_0 and U_1 at source line 180 come from this definition

standard_prerequisites.name: Elementary path counting in a locally finite graph
standard_prerequisites.statement: Path distance to a fixed set changes by at most one along consecutive vertices of an edge, and in a locally finite graph only finitely many vertices lie within distance 2d of a finite set
standard_prerequisites.use: Used at source lines 182 and 184 to force a ray out of the ball B(U_0,2d) and then to trap it in each annulus

core_obligations: Choose, from a Borel partition of X into U_0 and U_1 witnessing asi_B(G)=1 at the scale N=4d+1, the annuli V_i = A(U_0,2(i-1),2i) and the outer region W = X minus B(U_0,2d), and note that the V_i are pairwise disjoint Borel sets contained in U_1 (source line 180).

Prove that an injective G-ray cannot stay within distance 2d of U_0: otherwise the connecting vertices y_n for consecutive x_n lie in one G^{<=N}-component of U_0, hence form a finite set, and the ray then supplies infinitely many points within distance 2d of that finite set, contradicting local finiteness (source line 182).
Obtain the symmetric statement for U_0 by repeating the argument with the roles of U_0 and U_1 exchanged, so that the ray meets both pieces of the partition (source line 184).

Use that the distance to U_0 changes by at most one between consecutive vertices to find, for each 1 <= i <= d, a consecutive pair of the ray at distances 2i-1 and 2i from U_0, i.e. an edge inside V_i (source line 184).

Recover the announced 'infinitely many edges in each V_i' by applying the one-edge statement to every tail of the ray, using that a tail of an injective G-ray is again an injective G-ray (source line 178).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce the claim 'infinitely many edges in each V_i' to 'at least one edge in each V_i' for every tail, since a tail of an injective G-ray is again an injective G-ray.
Fix the two-piece Borel partition at scale N=4d+1 and define the annuli V_i and the outer region W.
Show that the ray must meet W, since otherwise the finite-component hypothesis on U_0 together with local finiteness is contradicted.
Get a meeting point of U_0 as well, and convert the unit-speed change of the distance to U_0 into one edge of the ray inside each V_i.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the article's Lemma lem:rainbow at source lines 173-175: from asi_B(G)=1 and a dimension d it must produce pairwise disjoint Borel sets V_i that every injective G-ray meets infinitely often. The construction can only be read off after fixing the two-piece Borel partition at the scale N=4d+1 and taking V_i = A(U_0,2(i-1),2i) (source line 180), and the real work is then to rule out the one way it could fail, namely a ray that keeps within distance 2d of U_0; that step needs the finite-component hypothesis on G^{<=N} restricted to U_0 together with local finiteness (source line 182) and a separate symmetric argument for U_0. Local combinatorics of a single ray does not give this, because the hypothesis is a global finiteness condition on distance-N components and the annuli exist only relative to a partition chosen beforehand; the change-of-distance-by-one step at line 184 is what finally converts a crossing of the two pieces into an edge inside every annulus.

dedup.scope: Same-source public primary and both claims already prepared from this source, plus the public identity index, the retired-claims record and the current worklist searched with the object names asymptotic separation index, asymptotic dimension, injective G-ray, annulus, rainbow and Borel edge coloring.

compared.difference: Same source, different proposition: lem:quotient (source lines 347-364) lifts an edge colouring of the Schreier graph of the quotient by a finite subgroup and re-colours the resulting two-orbit components. It contains no asymptotic separation index, no injective ray and no annulus construction.

Counts Theorem th:d+1 (source lines 84-86), the Vizing-type bound on the Borel edge chromatic number under asi_B=1. The present lemma is one of the two lemmas the author proves in order to obtain that bound, so it is upstream of it rather than a corollary; its conclusion is about rays and annuli, not about chromatic numbers.

Counts Theorem th:Z^d (source lines 98-105), the exact Borel edge chromatic numbers for Bernoulli actions of abelian groups; proved in Section 3 by protocol transitions, a different mechanism that never mentions rays or annuli.

editorial_scope: One original result: the article's Lemma lem:rainbow with its complete author proof, plus the article's own definitions of the Borel asymptotic separation index and of the ball and annulus notation used in that proof.
